commits.message:
Claim a never-attempted DA outbox row whatever the database clock

A seed writes each peer and announcement row with next_retry_at = NOW(),
and the claim later in the same pass required next_retry_at <= NOW().
When the database host's clock is stepped back between the two, as a
time sync does, the claim reads an earlier NOW() and skips the row: the
payload is delivered a whole pass late and the pass reports it as
backlog. A clock stepping back about 100 ms every 30 s did this to the
announcement in the corrupt-manifest rebase test.

A row with no attempt is now due at once; backoff starts with the first
recorded attempt, which always sets attempts to at least 1.

Refs #926

Point the doc references at the moved parity test and the deleted recovery

The SDK/Aiken schema parity test moved into the SDK package, and the
canonical journal recovery service was deleted with the stored own-block
status. The splitting reference now names the parity test's new path, and
the architecture plan marks its recovery citation as historical.

Screen forced rows that block processing writes and test the retired-event skip

Block processing now writes the rows of the retired events and spent
forced orders a processed landed block names, so the skip that leaves
every other retired event alone rests on a lookup, not on the query.
Tests now pin it for deposits, withdrawals and forced orders: an event
named only by a removed landed block, or by no block, gets no row and
no mempool projection. The withdrawal case runs through the production
replayer on a real block.

A forced order that processing wrote first used to skip the admission
divergence screen, because the forced-order hook only screens the rows
it writes itself. The screen is now one function in forced-orders/entry,
and both the hook and block processing call it with the hook's
divergence register, so the alarm reaches /readyz on either path.

recordNamedEvents and its types move to follower-events.named.ts, which
takes follower-events.ts and forced-orders/ingest.ts well below their
line limits and undoes the line-saving in ingest.

Refs #931

Delete the L1 control-plane source scans and bundle worker probes outside the package

Midgard Node CI on e71c6d22c failed in l1-control-plane-deleted.test.ts:
its scan of the node sources found the esbuild bundle that
intent-journal-worker-holds.test.ts was writing into the package root at
the same moment. Tests that scan source text or census the tree are
deleted when they go red, so that test goes, together with its docs
counterpart and the key list only those two read.

The two worker-thread tests now bundle their probe through one helper
that writes into the system temporary directory, with the package's
node_modules linked beside the bundle so its external imports still
resolve. No tree walk can find a probe bundle mid-run, and the copied
bundling setup lives in one place.

Carry an active own journal whose intent was pruned through 0037

The follower prunes an intent row once it has been terminal for k
blocks, and it does so during catch-up, before the node disposes of its
journals. A node that signs commit T, then is stopped for more than k
blocks after T settles on L1 (landed, expired, an input spent or a
dependency dead), restarts to find its active journal still naming T
while T's l1_intents row is gone. Disposition treats a pruned intent as
not dead, so the journal stays active, and migration 0037 refused it
with MIGRATION_0037_SIGNED_JOURNAL_WITHOUT_INTENT. Its hint could not
clear that refusal, so the node could not start without a hand edit.

Such a journal needs no refusal. After 0037 its status is derived from
the facts: landed or applied if its block landed, and otherwise dead
because its intent is no longer journaled, the reasoning the migration
already applies to applied and abandoned journals with pruned intents.
The journal keeps its intended hash, which satisfies the prepared-hash
check and keeps it out of the unsigned-journal discard. The refusal now
guards only a mismatch between the journal's signed bytes and an intent
row with the same hash, alongside the existing guards for a submitted
hash with no intended one and for a database with no intent journal.

Tests cover the carried journal in the pending and submitted states,
with and without a landed block, and a runtime case where the commit
tick resumes and prepares the next block once the live journal's
intent is pruned.

Compare the CPU sampler's process and thread totals in whole ticks

The check that the process total trails the main thread's by at most one
tick compared seconds rebuilt from tick counts. When the trail was
exactly one tick, the float products could put it a hair below the bound
(0.3 against 0.30000000000000004) and fail the test. Both totals are
whole ticks, so the test now compares them as ticks.

Name a DA publication hold on an unavailable DA manifest

The DA publication reconciler loads the DA manifest on every pass. When
it is missing or invalid, the pass seeds and delivers nothing and raises
da_publication_manifest_unavailable, which escalates after ten minutes.
The pass leaves the seeding cursor where it was and reports, as its
backlog, the stored payloads still awaiting outbox seeding. The first
pass with a valid manifest clears the reason and delivers every payload
held meanwhile, once to each committee peer.

The summary field that said whether the manifest loaded is renamed to
manifestLoaded. The comment on the seeding cursor now states how
delivery depends on its one-hour overlap: a query that also selected
every unseeded payload would scan the whole retention window on each
pass.

A test shows that a missing and a corrupt manifest each leave the rebase
applying the own block while delivery waits, and that delivery completes
once the manifest is restored.

Closes #926

Store an own landed block's DA payload without reading the DA manifest

The landed-block rebase seeded the payload's publication outboxes as it
applied the node's own block, which made it read the DA manifest inside
the rebase transaction. A missing or corrupt manifest therefore held the
rebase. The rebase now stores only the payload, and the DA publication
reconciler, which already seeds the outboxes from stored payloads, seeds
and delivers it.

The per-payload seeding helpers have no callers left and are deleted.
The module that now holds only the publication transport cache is
renamed to say so, and its unused publicationSatisfied is removed. The
tests that stubbed the manifest for the rebase no longer need to.

Refs #926

Delete the obsolete commit-parent-lease test size exception

Driving the production lifecycle through the intent journal brought
commit-parent-lease-emulator.test.ts to 498 lines, under the default
500-line limit, so its 590-line exception no longer applies.

Build the stack drill on the confirmed state when every block has merged

On an idle stack our node merges each attested block once it matures,
whoever holds the shift, so the state queue can hold only its root. The
drill read its predecessor, appended its blocks and checked its correction
evidence as if the queue always held a block, and twin4-long-2 failed at
its first family reading an empty queue.

A commit on an empty queue spends the root, and its header continues the
root's confirmed state (state-queue.ak:1157-1191, :124-138); a merge
writes the merged block's hash, UTxO root and end time into the root
(:401-409). So the drill now:

- reads the root as the settled, attested tail, rebuilding the block it
  holds from the authenticated transaction whose output the merge spent;
- appends after a block that merged by anchoring on the root, re-read at
  every commit attempt, in staging and in the transition trace;
- treats a block that left the queue by an authenticated merge as kept,
  in the predecessor, successor and removal-tail evidence;
- reads an attested history block that merged between polls as attested,
  and fails by name on a fault that merged before its fraud proof.

Arrange the commit-site tests for the derived journal status

Every commit tick now discards unsigned journals under the follower
write gate, so the commit-lease owner test opens the gate at a real
follower view rather than one no follower holds. The commit-base
resolver test's in-flight journal gets a commit anchor, without which
it derives dead and holds nothing.

Refs #806

Keep an own block's first landed time and clear it on a revert

The landed time was overwritten by every rebase that took the landing
in and was never cleared when a rebase reverted it, so a rolled-back
block still read as committed in the stress metrics. It is now kept
once stamped, and cleared in the same transaction as the rebase
deletes the reverted landed row, so a block that lands again is
stamped again.

The fork simulator's journal comparison leaves the column out: it is
wall-clock time for the metrics, which no derivation from the chain
reproduces. The stamp test now checks another journal stays unstamped
and that a revert clears the stamp.

Refs #806

Carry every submitted unjournaled commit through 0037

0037 copied the submitted hash into the intended one only for
abandoned journals. A journal of any status whose commit was submitted
without an intent journal entry records only its submitted hash, and
once that column goes it reads as unsigned; the next commit tick
discards every unsigned journal, so an applied or folded one would be
deleted. The copy now covers every row with a submitted hash and no
intended one, and a pending submission in that state is refused with
the other active ones.

A row whose prepared hash differs from its submitted one is refused by
name (MIGRATION_0037_SUBMITTED_COMMIT_NOT_PREPARED) instead of failing
the relaxed check. The migration test runs the unsigned-journal
discard after migrating and shows only the unsigned journal goes.

Refs #806

Keep the forced-order derivation free of the node's services

The forced-order derivation reached the node's services through
l1-admission-identity, which took its journal status fragments from
the derived-status reads: the determinism lint reported clocks, the
network and the host across 28 sites. The pure status and dead-header
SQL fragments move to pendingBlockFinalizations.status-sql.ts, and the
newest terminal outcome to l1-queue-terminals/terminal-outcome.ts;
derived-status keeps only the reads that need the database. Importers
take the fragments from their new home.

Refs #806

Record a foreign block's named events as it is processed

The foreign replay now returns the deposits, withdrawals and forced
orders it checked the block against, the forced rows built from the
field preimages its source check verified. Processing the block writes
the node's rows for them in the same transaction, so the rebase finds
every event the block names even after the follower has pruned it.
The rows match ingestion's byte for byte, and either write leaves the
other's row as it is.

The test covers all three kinds through rebaseIfDue on the real store:
a block processed now, one processed before this change whose event
retired unseen, and the row equality with ingestion.

Closes #931
